Overview heatmap of the species-level status of every variable

Source: R/plots.R
overview_heatmap.Rd

Variables in rows (there are many more of them than species), species in columns. Species are sorted most degraded first, variables by the number of species where they are critical, then warning.

Usage

overview_heatmap(
  overview,
  status_levels = c("Not tested", "Improved", "Warning", "Critical"),
  href = NULL
)

Arguments

overview

Data frame of the per-species rRMSE comparison (as exported to species_rrmse_comparison.csv), with columns species, variable, status, rrmse_ratio, rrmse_eval, rrmse_ref and n_obs.

status_levels

Statuses to show, in increasing order of severity.

href

Optional function of (species, variable, status) returning the URL opened when clicking each row's cell (NA for none).

Value

A plotly htmlwidget.

Examples

overview <- data.frame(
  species = rep(c("wheat", "maize"), each = 3),
  variable = rep(c("lai_n", "masec_n", "mafruit"), 2),
  status = c("Critical", "Improved", "Warning", "Improved", "Not tested",
             "Warning"),
  rrmse_ratio = c(12.4, -3.1, 2.7, -1.5, 0.8, 4.2),
  rrmse_eval = c(0.42, 0.25, 0.31, 0.18, 0.40, 0.29),
  rrmse_ref = c(0.37, 0.26, 0.30, 0.18, 0.40, 0.28),
  n_obs = c(120L, 85L, 64L, 97L, 8L, 51L)
)
overview_heatmap(overview)



# Open each species page when clicking a cell
overview_heatmap(
  overview,
  href = function(species, variable, status) {
    paste0("species/", species, ".html")
  }
)
